scenarios.name: test
scenarios.note: Mirrored about the plaza centre line (y = 1.0): four building removals, a pair of landmarks and a pair of solid screen walls. Found by search over the whole library scored on an even mixture of zone types plus matching north and south compositions. Result 25.6 / 5.3 / 24.0 / 45.0 % across the four reachable types, halves differing by 3.5 % (half L1), against a baseline of 68 / 0.3 / 10 / 21.5 % and 35.6 %. The removals are what keep "Open, facade-rich" alive: additive elements break facade continuity everywhere they are visible and collapse occlusivity, so a walls-only version of this scenario lost that type entirely (3.3 %). Zone 4 "Vast, regular" stays at 0 — it needs isovist area beyond what four removals free up.

scenarios.name: Rooms in the Square
scenarios.note: Four freestanding pavilions, 12 x 12 m at 7-9 m, staggered off-axis 25-30 m apart across the open middle. Intent: break the undifferentiated central plane into a sequence of inhabitable compartments. NOTE ON THE BRIEF: this was written to convert the square's "Vast, regular" ground, and Konstablerwache has none — that type holds 0 of 967 sampled points at baseline. What the pavilions actually convert is "Open, facade-rich", which is the undifferentiated centre the brief describes and which holds 68.0 % of the plaza. Result: 68.0 / 0.3 / 10.1 / 21.5 / 0 % becomes 2.0 / 0 / 18.7 / 79.3 / 0 %. Of the 658 zone-0 points, 121 are built over, 118 become "Tight, strongly enclosed" and 402 become "Tight, irregular". Enclosure rises 50.4 % within 20 m of a pavilion and only 4.9 % beyond, which is the compartment effect the brief predicted, localised as predicted. Occlusivity falls 29 % for the documented freestanding-continuity reason.

scenarios.name: Market Hall
scenarios.note: One 60 x 18 m hall at 8 m on the square's long east-west market axis, with a 6 x 6 m kiosk at either end at 4 m. The single-mass counterpart to "Rooms in the Square", drawn on the same selection against the same target so the two are directly comparable. Result: 4.5 / 0 / 45.7 / 49.8 / 0 %. It converts more of the open centre into "Tight, strongly enclosed" than four pavilions do (235 points against 118) and leaves a slightly more even spread (0.555 against 0.593 on half-L1 from an even five-way split) — but it reaches that partly by DELETING ground rather than changing it: 218 sampled positions are built over against 121. Enclosure rises 80.4 % within 20 m of the hall. Compactness is the one metric where the two diverge in kind: one large rectangular mass costs 2.1 %, four scattered ones cost 21.9 %, because a single convex obstacle does not serrate an isovist the way four separated ones do.

scenarios.name: Colonnaded Edge
scenarios.note: Three recessed arcades cut into three separate facades (north #63, south #89, west #164), 4 m deep, 28 m requested and 13.8 / 23.5 / 25.5 m actually cut — the recess holds one depth clear of each corner so its return walls meet open facade, which caps the opening at the facade length less 8 m. Plus a freestanding 40 m colonnade at 6 m along the east rim, where no facade qualifies for a recess. THE SHARPEST RESULT IN THE SET, and it splits: the recesses ALONE take "Open, facade-rich" from 68.0 % to 93.3 %, raising occlusivity 15.0 %, area 1.1 % and solidity 1.2 % — the only intervention in the library that strengthens a zone instead of diluting it, and the only one that improves three metrics at once. The added colonnade ALONE does the opposite: compactness -54.9 %, zone 0 down to 12.0 %. Together the colonnade wins (29.4 % zone 0, compactness -57.6 %), because nothing the recesses add can offset serration on that scale. The change propagates: occlusivity rises 15.5 % at the rim and 14.4 % in the centre, but reclassification does not — 40 % of rim points change type against 10 % in the centre, because centre points were already deep inside zone 0 and a strengthened zone 0 is still zone 0.

scenarios.name: Shaded Grove
scenarios.note: Two rows of eight trees at 6 m spacing, canopy 7 m across topping out at 5 m; a 30 x 12 m canopy on 600 mm piers at 6 m, built as two parallel colonnade runs 12 m apart because the pergola preset's posts are fixed at 250 mm and the colonnade's are 600 mm; and a 20 m raised step platform along the east side. Result: 2.1 / 0 / 0.1 / 97.8 / 0 %. WHAT MOVED AND WHAT DID NOT: solidity -17.5 % and area -19.3 % are the real changes; occlusivity -20.0 % is real and in the documented direction; enclosure +2.7 % is nothing; compactness -84.5 % is the spurious thin-element collapse this phase added solidity to replace, and must not be read as a finding. The steps register EXACTLY nothing — zero change on all six metrics, zero points dropped — because at 0.9 m they sit under the 1.6 m measured slice, which is the preset predicting its own result. Neither do the canopies: at 2.5 m clearance the foliage floats above the slice and only 400 mm trunks are counted, so this scenario measures a grove's trunks and has no way at all to register its shade.

scenarios.name: Bridging the Level Break
scenarios.note: Three station-head pavilions, 14 x 10 m at 6-7 m, each flanking one of the square's existing transport accesses rather than standing in open ground; 10 m raised step platforms on the square-facing side of each; one 20 m screen wall at 2.6 m closing the exposed gap between the two eastern pavilions. The accesses were read off the model, not assumed: three 3.2 m structures stand inside the plaza (#100 at 21.5,-20.8; #161 at 18.1,19.6; #162 at -18.5,29.6) and each punches a matching hole in the standable lattice, which is the fragmentation the brief describes, visible in the data. Result: 68.0 / 0.3 / 10.1 / 21.5 / 0 % becomes 10.2 / 9.3 / 23.1 / 57.4 / 0 %. TWO RESULTS THAT NO OTHER SCENARIO PRODUCES. First, compactness RISES 9.7 % — every other additive scenario lowers it, "Rooms in the Square" by 21.9 %. A control settles why: the same three pavilions, same footprints and heights, moved into open ground away from the accesses give compactness -19.9 % instead of +8.4 %, a 28-point swing from position alone. Consolidating mass against an existing obstruction absorbs it into one silhouette where the same mass in open ground adds a second, independent notch to the isovist. Second, "Open, regular" goes from 3 points to 82 (0.3 % to 9.3 %) — the only scenario in the set to reach that type at all, and the displaced control reaches 0.0 % of it. Against "Rooms in the Square": the changes here CLUSTER on the accesses (57 % of reclassified points lie within 30 m of one, against 46 % of the plaza) where Rooms' changes are exactly proportional to area (49 % against 49 %) — scattered, by the measurement. Bridging yields 17 distinct zone patches against Rooms' 13, and its largest single patch is 406 points against 670: more differentiated structure, not less.

scenarios.name: Zeil Terminus
scenarios.note: One 20 x 20 m landmark at 15 m closing the Zeil axis at the east end, with two 35 m colonnades at 6 m compressing the western approach to a 14 m throat. Axis direction taken from the register rather than assumed: the Zeil site centre lies 417 m due west of Konstablerwache's, so the square is its eastern terminus and the gesture faces west. Result: 2.3 / 0 / 4.5 / 93.2 / 0 %. THE HEIGHT TEST, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS SCENARIO, AND IT IS CLEAN. Holding footprint and position identical and varying only height, the 20 x 20 mass alone gives: area -18.1 % at both 8 m and 15 m, compactness +5.9 % at both, enclosure 9.9 % against 16.9 %. Height moves enclosure and NOTHING else, to four significant figures — the first controlled confirmation in this phase that the other three metrics are pure plan geometry. Near the mass the effect nearly doubles: +47.5 % against +67.4 % within 25 m, +2.5 % against +7.0 % beyond. And it converts: "Tight, strongly enclosed" reaches 24.3 % at 8 m and 33.3 % at 15 m. BUT THE FULL SCENARIO DESTROYS ITS OWN RESULT. The landmark alone leaves the best-balanced plaza of any scenario here (21.8 / 5.6 / 24.3 / 48.3 % at 8 m, 19.5 / 3.5 / 33.3 / 43.7 % at 15 m); adding the two colonnades takes compactness to -75.7 % and flattens everything to 93.2 % "Tight, irregular". Half against half, split at x = -18: the compressed western half goes to 99.1 % one type, the terminus half to 84.2 % but keeping 11.4 % enclosed. Directional compression built from columns does not compress, it serrates. The single tall mass produces a stronger and more legible enclosure shift than four dispersed mid-rise masses or one long low one; the threshold that was supposed to reinforce it is what erases it. NOTE ON THE BRIEF: it asks whether height converts "Vast, regular" to "Tight, strongly enclosed". This plaza holds 0 points of "Vast, regular", so the conversion measured is out of "Open, facade-rich".
